Hi everyone, I drafted a PR #36439 to help reduce boilerplate when working with A[x], but I'd like a quick sanity check on the design.

I find myself constantly writing ⟨x, Algebra.self_mem_adjoin_singleton A x⟩ or ⟨p.aeval x, aeval_mem_adjoin_singleton A x⟩. To fix this, I added CoeDep instances for both x and p.aeval x so that we can simply write (x : A[x]) and (p.aeval x : A[x]). You can get a feel of what this would look like in this PR #37723. I personally like this because it closely what I have on paper : Given some x : A, writing x when the expected type is R[X] is fine because there is some obvious map to be inserted to see x : A as an element of R[x].

Because this uses CoeDep for specific values rather than a full type-to-type coercion, I know it's a bit non-standard. Hence this discussion.

Do people think this is a good idea? Does anyone foresee this causing issues with simp or typeclass resolution down the line? Any feedback is appreciated!

Pinging the people that left a review: @Anne Baanen @Christian Merten @Johan Commelin
This seems probably ok to me, and I certainly see the appeal
:search: CoeDep, decPropToBool, and 9 more
I don't know how difficult this is but could you generalise to finite sets? As with docs#IntermediateField.adjoin
Regarding my loogle links above: seemingly we have a number of CoeDep instances which aren't actually dependent!
@Artie Khovanov What do you have in mind?
Ah! For R[x,y,z]? I can see it for x : R[x,y,z], y : R[x,y,z] and z : R[x,y,z]but for an evaluated multivariate poly idk
Another answer here would be to declare that the preferred spelling is ⟨x, by grind⟩
Yes if we don't want the CoeDeps this will probably be my preferred choice.

Ah! For R[x,y,z]? I can see it for x : R[x,y,z], y : R[x,y,z] and z : R[x,y,z]but for an evaluated multivariate poly idk

yeah sorry I just mean that

I don't think docs#IntermediateField.adjoin even has the coercions - I just mean the nice R[x,y,z] notation.
If this is fine I will remove the awaiting Zulip from #36439. I'll do that later tonight if there are no complaints about doing this :)
I don't think this is what @Artie Khovanov meant but currently only x : R[x] is supported. I can add something for supporting x : R[x,y,z], y : R[x,y,z] and z : R[x,y,z] if people would like that!

That would be cool, if it isn't too much of a perf hit
And yeah I didn't know notation for Algebra.adjoin had been added.
@Eric Wieser Could I ask your opinion on the generalization to many variables I implemented? That is, the support for xₖ : R[x₁, ..., xₙ]. See the commit here.
It's cute but I think probably not a good idea
